title: The Nature of Being
subtitle: The future lies ahead, but will it bring new advancements or devastation?

items.speaker: X
items.text: Hm ...

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: That is unexpected.
As the trio return from the stage, they notice that what they intended to bring has disappeared, and in its stead is a Chirper.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Is this the hydrogen cell that you mentioned?

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: It does have a very unique appearance for a power cell, though I take it that this may be a consequence of the alternate technology involved.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: No. It's not a power cell. Just a talking pocket watch.

items.speaker: X
items.text: Ahaha! What a remarkable outcome! The object changed entirely during the transfer. I guess this is another fascinating aspect of the stage. An unaccounted variable, like the Butterfly Effect.

items.speaker: X
items.text: A hydrogen cell turned into a Chirper ... The science of that alone is worth studying, hah, don't you think?

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Indeed. I am immediately curious what effect the stage might have on my own body if I attempted to travel through it.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Would my robotic shell change to fit the local culture and technology of the destination, just as it did Vertin's outfit?

items.speaker: X
items.text: Why not give it a try and find out? I can activate it again anytime. It's about time you took a vacation, Madam Lucy.

items.speaker: Left
items.text: Should you intend to visit again, I will make certain to register you as legal visitors.
Left and Right appear on the communicator's screen.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Thank you for your offer, but I am afraid I have to decline.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: I believe our team is in need of an immediate physical examination after the events they have gone through, in particular, to determine the effects of a certain injection.

items.speaker: X
items.text: Ahaha, ah. Personally, I'm entirely intrigued by the possibility of keeping this polymer in my bloodstream.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Your well-being is top priority in this particular matter, Researcher X.

items.speaker: X
items.text: Ah, can we make it short? The stage could change its destination anytime.

items.speaker: X
items.text: I don't want to ruin Madam Lucy's prospects for a vacation.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: You'll need a thorough examination, I'm afraid. We can't run the risk that the polymer shifted during travel as well. You can tell Lucy all about our findings while you recuperate at the rehab center.

items.speaker: X
items.text: *sigh* Fine, fine. You're the boss.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: While I am intrigued by the prospect of traveling, the changing destinations of the stage do not follow fixed patterns. I am willing to "roll the dice," as you might say.

items.speaker: Mesmer Jr.
items.text: I'll get X to the rehab center and make sure he stays put. Why don't you spend some time here while you can, Madam Lucy?
The young visitors organize their reports and set off for the rehab center.
Soon the laboratory quiets down.

items.speaker: Left
items.text: There appears to be a strong rapport between you and your researchers.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: It pleases me to hear you say that. I will take that as a marked improvement of my understanding of humanitarianism.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: From my cursory reading of Vertin's report, I have already learned a great deal about your world.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Despite running dozens of simulated scenarios, I still find it hard to pinpoint the divergence between our worlds' respective technological progression—another fascinating element of scientific discovery.

items.speaker: Right
items.text: Scientific development is often shaped by the demands of the environment. Perhaps the unique struggles of your world led to a divergence in technological need, just as they did in ours.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: If I have learned anything from humans, it is that their greatest motivation is and has always been survival. It is admirable even if it can lead science towards destructive paths.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: The greatest danger lies in giving up and dwelling in the mistakes of the past.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: I have lived through many generations of human technology and observed their progress firsthand. Setbacks and disasters are inevitable, but there will always be those willing to take risks to bring about a better world.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Innovation is a process that feels in many ways like laying track before a speeding train. Too often, we only see the hazards ahead when it is too late to change course.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: But as long as humanity survives, they will learn from those harsh lessons and overcome.

items.speaker: Left
items.text: Analysis: Your theory of human progress bears a strong resemblance to the process of natural selection.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Perhaps so. But the random dictates of genetic mutation are a much slower process. I have seen human innovation leapfrog eons of natural development within a single generation. I am excited to see where they will go next.
Lucy removes her human mask, revealing her expressionless metallic face beneath. Yet the red light pulses, pondering the future.
In that moment, standing on the bridge between two worlds, two forms of inorganic life discuss the very nature of being.
